The U.S. Coast Guard is searching the waters off south of Nantucket, Massachusetts
for a Canadian air ambulance that disappeared early today
while traveling from Bermuda to Boston.

The Gulfstream G-100 is believed to have been carrying six people on board
when it lost contact with air traffic control, according to the Coast Guard.
Flight data show the jet dropped at least 9,000 feet over two minutes,
then leveled off for several more minutes before disappearing.
The pilot declared an emergency, according to Nantucket Memorial Airport.
During an exchange, air traffic control asked the pilot of the air ambulance,

A fire rescue dispatcher warned emergency crews.

The Coast Guard has deployed two search and rescue planes,

Frank Langford, NPR News.
The U.S. says citizens needing help in Brazil should not come to its embassy
or consular facilities.
It's an unusual suspension that comes as Brazilians go to the polls.
Citing unspecified security concerns,
the U.S. announced the closure of its diplomatic missions beginning Friday.
The U.S. State Department did not say what prompted the closures,
nor when consular services would resume operations.
Federal police in Brazil said they had not found evidence of a threat
after carrying out preventative searches in Sao Paulo and near Brasilia.
The presidential race pits incumbent leftist Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva

the son of former far-right President Jair Bolsonaro,

Carrie Khan, NPR News, Rio de Janeiro.

A new study shows that eating with another person
may help you manage your blood sugar.
As NPR's Burley McCoy reports,
researchers gave two groups of participants the same amount of bread to eat,
then measured how their blood sugar rose and recovered.
In one group, the participants ate their bread alone.
In the other, someone else was in the room,
and they found the social eaters recovered quicker.
That is, their blood sugar didn't spike as high
or came back down quicker, or both.
Lead author and behavioral neuroscientist Shir Adziel says
this might be because humans are social animals.
If my brain develops in a social context,
my brain learns to regulate my glucose levels in social proximity.
She says other people may be a social cue the brain uses
to start processing sugar earlier,
for example, by releasing insulin, which helps regulate blood sugar.
The results appear in the journal Science Advances,
Burley McCoy, NPR News.
A National Guard member deployed to Washington, D.C.
as part of President Trump's initiative

The Associated Press reports specialist Jacob Noonan
was arrested after a traffic stop by U.S. Park Police
and charged with that gun-related offense.
Noonan was off-duty, not in uniform,
and driving his personal vehicle at the time.
This is the second time in two months
that a member of the task force has been arrested.
The presence of National Guard members in Washington
has been contentious since the deployment began in August of 2025.
I'm Lyndi Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.
